description.value: Greendrop Lake is a hike-in wilderness camp tucked among old-growth forest and subalpine terrain in Sx̱ótsaqel/Chilliwack Lake Park; a backcountry permit and fee are required in advance, and no fires are allowed.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The OSM record identifies Greendrop Lake Camp as a backcountry tent-only campsite within Sx̱ótsaqel/Chilliwack Lake Provincial Park, operated by BC Parks. The park website confirms it is one of four backcountry camps in the park requiring a backcountry registration permit, that open fires are prohibited in the backcountry, and that the site is accessed by trail — corroborating OSM tags (backcountry=yes, openfire=no, tents=yes). The website URL in OSM matches the fetched page, though no dedicated Greendrop-specific sub-page exists, so some site-level amenity details cannot be individually verified beyond OSM tags.
concerns: OSM website URL points to the parent park page (Sx̱ótsaqel/Chilliwack Lake Park) rather than a dedicated Greendrop Lake Camp page; amenity details specific to this camp cannot be fully verified.
No phone, email, or physical address is available in OSM or on the website for this specific camp.
Site is trail-access only; no cycling or bike access is mentioned anywhere in OSM tags or website content.

OSM tag reservation=no, but the BC Parks website states backcountry registration (permit) is required and can be completed online in advance — the distinction between permit registration and reservation is ambiguous for directory purposes.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Greendrop Lake Camp is a remote backcountry campsite accessible only by hiking trail with no road or confirmed cycling access, making its fit for a cycling tourism directory dependent on whether the WWC scope includes backcountry or bikepacking destinations.
enrichment_extras.notes: The BC Parks backcountry permit page states permits cannot sell out, suggesting this is a registration/fee system rather than a capacity-limited reservation system; the OSM reservation=no tag is likely accurate in the traditional sense.
